name: GRAMMER AG
brief: Railway passenger seats; evaluating them for a regional train order.
summary: GRAMMER AG maps material flows through Tier 3 using IMDS and RMI templates but has not confirmed comprehensive visibility into Tier 4 and beyond, relying on a global multi‑tier supply chain for raw materials. [4] [1] A mandatory Supplier Code of Conduct has been required in every digital RFQ since 2017, with 100 % of global suppliers confirming it, and formal VDA 6.3 process audits are conducted globally with annual internal supplier audits. [2] [3] Digital risk management via SPHERA‑SCM provides annual data updates for ongoing monitoring. [3] The company achieved a 25 % reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2024, reports a group recycling rate of 85.73 % and targets over 75 % product recyclability, while aiming for net‑zero operational emissions by 2040 without disclosed Scope 3 interim targets. [8] [9] Financially, GRAMMER AG returned to profitability with EUR 17.2 M net income in FY 2025 after a EUR 115.2 M loss, but carries high debt (non‑current liabilities EUR 719.1 M, current liabilities EUR 623.9 M) and a low equity ratio of 18.1 %, with loan covenants suspending dividends until 2027. [6] [7]

insights.headline: Profitability restored but leverage remains high and dividends blocked until 2027.
Sub‑tier visibility stops at Tier 3; Tier 4 mapping not yet confirmed despite mandatory SCoC and annual VDA audits.
Continuous digital risk monitoring (SPHERA‑SCM) and yearly VDA 6.3 audits give periodic oversight of supplier practices.
Climate progress: 25 % Scope 1&2 cut by 2024, 85.73 % recycling, 2040 net‑zero goal, but no public Scope 3 interim targets.
Equity ratio only 18.1 %, indicating a thin capital buffer despite recent profit.
Supplier Code of Conduct mandatory since 2017 with 100 % global supplier sign‑off.

report.headline: GRAMMER AG maps materials to Tier 3 but lacks confirmed comprehensive visibility into Tier 4 and beyond.

findings.text: GRAMMER AG uses the International Material Data System (IMDS) and RMI templates (CMRT/EMRT) to map material flows and conflict minerals through Tier 3 of its supply chain.
Deeper Tier 4 mapping is explicitly noted as not yet confirmed as comprehensive, leaving a gap in visibility for raw-material extraction and sub-supplier levels.
The company relies on a global, multi-tier supply chain for raw materials including metals, plastics, textiles, and foams, making sub-tier transparency a critical operational requirement.
A Supplier Code of Conduct (SCoC) has been mandatory in every digital RFQ since 2017, and 100% of global suppliers are required to confirm it, extending contractual expectations down the chain.
Formal process audits (VDA 6.3) are conducted globally and suppliers must perform internal audits at least annually, providing a periodic check on sub-tier practices.
Digital risk management via SPHERA-SCM provides annual data updates, supporting ongoing monitoring rather than one-off assessments.

What escalation process exists if a Tier 4 supplier refuses disclosure or fails an audit?

report.headline: GRAMMER AG shows improved profitability but carries high debt and low equity; loan covenants restrict dividends until 2027

findings.text: The company reported a net income of EUR 17.2 million for the 2025 financial year, reversing a net loss of EUR 115.2 million in the prior year, indicating a return to profitability.
Accumulated losses from the previous financial year mean no dividend is currently proposed, and a renewed loan agreement in 2024 explicitly suspends dividend payments until 2027.
As of the latest reporting date, the equity ratio stands at 18.1%, up 0.8 percentage points, but remains low, signaling a thin capital buffer.
Non-current liabilities are high at EUR 719.1 million and current liabilities rose 2.8% to EUR 623.9 million, showing a heavy debt load with growing short-term obligations.

openQuestions: What are the specific financial covenants attached to the loan agreement renewed in 2024, and is the company currently in compliance?
